memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The sons of Leah: Reuben the firstborn of Jacob, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar and Zebulun. The sons of Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin. The sons of Rachel's servant Bilhah: Dan and Naphtali. The sons of Leah's servant Zilpah: Gad and Asher. These were the sons of Jacob, who were born to him in Paddan Aram." - Gen 35:23-26 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here the twelve sons of Jacob are listed together — the men who would become the twelve tribes of Israel, the nation through whom God would bless the world. It is a significant list. From these twelve would come the whole people of Israel, and eventually, from the tribe of Judah, the Messiah Himself.

But pause and consider what kind of family this really was. We have watched it up close through many chapters: rivalry between wives, favouritism, deception, jealousy, the violence of Simeon and Levi at Shechem, the sin of Reuben. This is no picture-perfect, holy family. It is a deeply flawed, often broken household. And yet — this is the family God chose to build His nation and bring His salvation into the world.

What grace this reveals. God does not wait for perfect people or perfect families to accomplish His purposes. He takes flawed, struggling, sinful people and weaves His redemption right through them. If God could build the nation of Israel — and bring the Saviour — through a family like this, then no life and no family is beyond His use.

Whatever your family's failings, whatever your own, take heart. God specialises in working through imperfect people. He is not looking for the flawless; He is looking for those He can shape by His grace. He can write His good purposes through your story too.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I believe God can work through my flawed family and me?
2. How does the messiness of this family magnify God's grace?
3. Where have I disqualified myself that God has not?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You build Your purposes through flawed and imperfect people. Where my family and I fall short, work Your grace, and use my life for Your good purposes. Amen.
